A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across appendix reorganization and figure renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original benchmark, input-perturbation and medical-domain experiments, including accuracy/F1, divergence metrics, overlap analysis and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4.1–4.3 and the appendices, including Tables 1–6 and 10–12.

M1.justification: The evaluated acceleration procedures and models are unchanged. V4 introduces no algorithmic component, architecture modification, training objective or revised inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten general multimodal benchmarks, biomedical conversation test set and VQA-RAD, including the same visual/text perturbation scenarios. Industrial, longitudinal and deployment evaluations mentioned in v4 are future work.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same token-reduction and quantization methods, including the medical-domain subset (Tables 1–6 and 10–12). Newly cited LVPruning is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and sample counts, evaluation metrics, model sizes, quantization settings and token-reduction configurations are retained. Both versions use the same 87 textual and 96 visual perturbation configurations and matched perturbed inputs.

E4.justification: The perturbation tests, medical case studies and divergence-overlap analysis are unchanged. V4's standalone Appendix D reproduces the overlap analysis previously within v3's Data Visualisation appendix; its heatmap changes from Figure 4 to Figure 3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained distribution plots display benchmark/method scores without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Numerical tables, plotted results, overlap values and qualitative examples are retained after relocation. For example, VisionZip on LLaVA-Med still reports DR 29.85% and NDR 5.12% on VQA-RAD in Table 6.

T1.justification: The DR, NDR and medical evaluation metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and central claims: small aggregate performance changes conceal instance-level instability, with perturbation and medical-domain evidence. The rewritten conclusion preserves these scientific claims.

C2.justification: V3 already cautions against industrial extrapolation. V4 explicitly qualifies external/ecological validity, identifies natural drift and operational constraints, and specifies future deployment validation. Section 5 also adds concrete recommendations for DR/NDR reporting, documented perturbations and critical-instance testing.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain the same dataset details, token-reduction hyperparameters and perturbation procedure. No hardware, runtime, code availability or data-access information is added; the new caption citations repeat existing perturbation attribution.

R1.justification: V4 adds introductory references to Lanvikd, BRIDGE and LVPruning, plus a 'Silent hazards of token reduction' reference bearing this paper's arXiv identifier. Section 2's substantive positioning and the claimed novelty remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 5–6 are rewritten and expanded, and the existing overlap analysis becomes a separate appendix before Data Visualisation. Most prose remains unchanged. Section 3.4's correct Appendix C reference becomes an incorrect Appendix A reference.

P2.justification: V3 Figures 2 and 3 become side-by-side panels of v4 Figure 2 with a shared caption. The unchanged heatmap and examples are relocated and renumbered; Tables 8–9 gain attribution in their captions. Appendix layout changes without new graphical evidence.

improvement.justification: Sections 5–6 modestly improve practical guidance and qualification: v3's broad stability-check recommendation becomes explicit reporting/testing recommendations, with clearer industrial-validation gaps and proposed drift/deployment studies. The empirical evidence remains unchanged. These limited gains are partly offset by the newly incorrect Appendix A pointer for perturbation details in Section 3.4.
